slides.heading: Year 1 — Autumn 1, Week 3
slides.sub: New content taught directly, practised in words/sentences and applied in reading and dictation.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ue" (/uː/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-90 -110 180 180" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="glue" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="wp-icon" data-picture="glue"><rect x="-45" y="-56" width="90" height="56" rx="6" ry="6" fill="#c3ced6" stroke="#3b4954" stroke-width="3.5"/><rect x="-59" y="-39.2" width="14" height="10" rx="6" ry="6" fill="#c3ced6" stroke="#3b4954" stroke-width="2.5"/><rect x="45" y="-39.2" width="14" height="10" rx="6" ry="6" fill="#c3ced6" stroke="#3b4954" stroke-width="2.5"/><ellipse cx="0" cy="-56" rx="45" ry="8" fill="#c3ced6" stroke="#3b4954" stroke-width="2.5"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Dewey Raindrop streaks down the window pane leaving a shiny trail and a soft 'ue' as he goes.

character.name: Dewey Raindrop
character.blurb: Dewey Raindrop is a sky-blue drop with one shiny streak down his middle, and he trails a long 'ue' sound as he slides.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'oo' in moon — 'ue' usually appears at the end of a word.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'u', then 'e', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children trace a finger down an imaginary window pane while saying a long 'ue' sound.

slides.dictation: A blue jay sits in the tree.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "aw" (/ɔː/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="paw print" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="paw_print_icon"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Hawthorn Hedgehog stretches out one spiky claw and scrapes it slowly along the ground, saying 'aw' as he goes.

character.name: Hawthorn Hedgehog
character.blurb: Hawthorn Hedgehog has sandy spines dotted with little spots, and he drags one claw along the path, saying 'aw' with every scrape.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'or' in for — 'aw' usually appears at the end of a word.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'a', then 'w', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children curl one hand into a claw shape and scrape it slowly through the air, saying 'aw'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="paw print" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="paw_print_icon"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.dictation: A paw print is in the mud.

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "tch" (/tʃ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.mnemonic: Catch it at the end: after a short vowel, /ch/ is usually spelt t-c-h, as in catch, fetch and kitchen.
slides.pronunciation_note: Another way to write the /ch/ sound children already know from 'chip' — the t is silent. 'tch' comes straight after a short vowel at the end of a word: catch, fetch, kitchen. (Common exceptions: rich, which, much, such.)
slides.formation_cue: Write 't', then 'c', then 'h', close together — three letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children pretend to catch a ball with both hands, saying 'ch' as they catch it.

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Extra practice blending and segmenting everything taught this week — no new content today.

slides.dictation: The glue is stuck to the desk.

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.

slides.dictation: The straw hat is on the shelf.
